newsitem.title: FRANCE: KLM seen chosing Lyon as freighter sub-hub.
newsitem.headline: KLM seen chosing Lyon as freighter sub-hub.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV is poised to choose Lyon-Satolas airport as the site of its proposed freighter sub-hub in eastern France, industry sources told Reuters.
No one at KLM's regional cargo office in Paris was immediately available to comment on the reports.
A Lyon-Satolas official confirmed that the airport authority would be meeting with KLM executives next week to discuss the project.
"We have been in negotiations with KLM for some time but we cannot comment on reports that KLM has chosen Lyon."
KLM had told the airport at a previous meeting it would make its decision by end June 1997, the official added.

Last year, Lyon-Satolas handled 21,509 tonnes, compared to 19,586 tonnes in 1995, while the KLM sub-hub might eventually in the long-term generate by itself 30,000 to 50,000 tonnes of cargo, industry officials said.

Dijon's Chamber of Commerce told Reuters earlier this year the city's airport was the subject of negotiations with KLM but confirmed on Thursday it was now out of the running as the freighter sub-hub.
Sources at both Basle-Mulhouse and Strasbourg airports said there had been contact with KLM over the project but could not say whether formal discussions had taken place.

In an interview with Reuters earlier this year, KLM Cargo's Paris-based Operations manager, Southern Europe, Simon Groenenboom, said KLM Cargo planned to set-up a sub-hub serving France, Switzerland, Germany, northern Italy and Luxembourg, offering direct freighter connections to the Far East and the U.S..
"This would take the pressure off our Schiphol hub while at the same time realising important economies of scale and providing greater proximity in terms of customer service," Groenenboom had said.

The sub-hub could be in the first phase of service by 1999 with a full-term objective being an annual throughput of traffic between 30,000 to 50,000 tonnes, he had then added, but declined to comment on the specific sites under consideration.
The only scheduled all-cargo flights to operate from Lyon-Satolas are those for overnight express traffic
Air France suspended scheduled Boeing 747-200F services from the airport in 1993 but continues to use Lyons for full-freighter shipments of Beaujolais Nouveau each November.

Extension work to Lyon-Satolas' freight terminal is due to start next month with 3,500 sq metres of warehousing and 1,300 sq metres of offices being added to existing facilities covering around 25,000 sq metres.
The airport, which is also open 24 hours a day, is equipped with a high-speed TGV rail link.
